To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
The most common litter items found on beaches are plastic and cigarette butts and filters, with a total contribution of over 50% in 2014 and over 60% in 2015, 2016, 2017.

(1) The Romanian Black Sea Coast is affected by litter, especially plastic and cigarettes butts and filters, (2) the amount of litter increased in 2016 2017, compared to the 2014 15 period and (3) the main sources of litter are tourism and urbanization.
the Romanian Black Sea coast suffers from marine litter pollution, and the most abundant items were plastic, polystyrene and cigarette butts.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification of the main litter items and the main sources of litter in the Romanian Black Sea sandy beaches.
the identification of marine litter types, the assessment of their abundance, and the analysis of their seasonal and spatial variability in sandy littoral.
the assessment of the occurrence of marine litter in the littoral zone of sandy beaches situated at the Romanian Black Sea.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the Romanian Black Sea coast has a serious problem with litter, especially plastic litter, that needs to be urgently addressed.

the Romanian Black Sea coast is not a clean environment; the litter amount is higher in summer than in winter, the litter composition is dominated by plastic and cigarette butts and filters; the litter amount increases in the proximity of the cities; the litter amount varies from year to year; and the litter amount increases with the number of tourists.
the Romanian littoral is affected by a high level of marine litter.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
plastic litter is a serious problem on the Romanian littoral, with the highest concentrations being found in the sectors situated near urbanized areas, such as Mangalia 4 and Eforie.
the Romanian Black Sea beaches suffer from the same problem as the other European coasts, and that the problem of marine litter has to be addressed at national level.
the Romanian littoral is not free of marine litter.
The main takeaway from our work is that
litter occurrence is higher in the most touristic and urbanised sectors, and it is higher during the summer period, which is the most touristic one, than during the winter.
litter is an issue that should be addressed by all stakeholders involved in the management of the marine environment, including local communities and tourists.

marine litter monitoring should be carried out on a regular basis and that a long time series of data is needed to identify the sources of marine litter and to assess its temporal and spatial distribution.
